mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in periods where FEDFUNDS exceeds 5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening household demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) when UNRATE exceeds 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) during four consecutive months of industrial production contraction relative to its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above 3% for two consecutive months signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and raises discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed 3% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals a recovery in residential investment, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.05 z-score) when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a two-month period indicates a mixed labor market where job creation is insufficient to lower unemployment, which signals policy uncertainty and muted earnings growth, resulting in flat or negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE increases over 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) when PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and reduced consumer spending, which depresses retail and discretionary equities and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) when RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months.
